desc:
In one move you may change a single character of s into any lowercase letter. Return the minimum number of moves after which the word t appears in s as a contiguous block of characters.

The length of s cannot change, so if t is longer than s the answer is -1.

s = "abcdef", t = "cxe"  ->  1   (change d to x)
s = "aaaa",   t = "aa"   ->  0
s = "ab",     t = "abc"  -> -1
s = "xyxy",   t = "yy"   ->  1
constraints: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters
hints: Whatever you do, the final string contains t starting at some position. Pick that position first.
Once the start position is fixed, the cost is the number of aligned pairs where the characters differ. Different start positions do not interact.
Try every start from 0 to len(s) - len(t), count mismatches in that window, and keep the smallest count.
editorial: Only replacements are allowed, so the characters of s never shift: if t ends up starting at index i, then s[i + k] must become t[k] for every k. Each position already equal costs nothing and each other position costs exactly one replacement. The windows are independent, so the answer is the minimum over all start positions of the number of mismatches (the Hamming distance between t and the window).

There are len(s) - len(t) + 1 windows and each costs len(t) comparisons, so the total is at most about n²/4 comparisons, fine for 2,000 characters. When insertions and deletions are also allowed the windows stop being aligned and the problem becomes the approximate substring search solved with a table.
